nodes.description: ASCT1 takes D-serine up into astrocytes and supplies neurons with the L-serine from which D-serine is made. The constitutive Slc1a4 null mouse has lower brain D-serine and higher glycine, with a shift in the relative contributions of D-serine and glycine to NMDA receptor activity. The D-serine deficit is shown in the null mouse and not in the knock-in carrying the common p.Glu256Lys allele: the mutant transporter has a higher affinity and a lower maximal rate for D-serine, knock-in brain slices take up D-serine faster at physiological concentrations, and hippocampal long-term potentiation is normal. Brain D-serine levels were not measured in the knock-in. Whether this axis contributes to the human phenotype, as opposed to the L-serine deficit, is unsettled.
